stop_status: CLEAR. One confirmed UB-class hidden obligation (B29-D1) was found and repaired: the signal handler and the main thread shared a plain `static mut int` for `intr_signal`. It is now `static INTR_SIGNAL: AtomicI32` with relaxed store/load, so the handler's only operation is a lock-free atomic store and no `static mut` is reachable from the signal edge. A real-SIGUSR1 control observes the handler's store; the SIGINT mapping and the read-buffer cleanse are each proved by a temporary negative control that made the new test fail, after which the exact blob 7f43920ed93d52607039a2125cbd6e44dbe0b38b was restored. A second, low-severity secret-residue defect (B29-D2, the uncleansed over-long-line tail in `read_till_nl`) is repaired as a recorded §5 divergence. No ABI, `#[repr(C)]` layout, export, signature, allocator seam or lint attribute changed. No memory-safety defect remains; no safe-Rust caller can cause UB. The file-level classification is CONTRACTED, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED, because B29-UI-4's registry concurrency remains an explicitly stated caller obligation with no independent dynamic check.

external_contracts: A process runs at most one console session at a time: tty_in, tty_out, is_a_tty, savsig, ps and tty_orig/tty_new are process-global, as the authority declares them. Concurrent UI_process calls over the default method would race on these cells; the precondition is stated in the module header and is the same serialisation the authority's unsynchronised globals require.

UI_set_default_method is documented by the authority as not thread-safe and must not be called at the same time as other OpenSSL functions; the port's plain non-atomic load/store relies on that documented contract.
UI_OpenSSL returns a *mut to the same 'static method object UI_get_default_method shares; mutating that object must be ordered before publication (a caller obligation, now stated at the export).
write_string/read_string run only inside UI_process between open_session and close_session, so TTY_OUT/TTY_IN point at the session's streams.

Constructors establish the callback's string preconditions: general_allocate_prompt rejects a NULL prompt, UI_add_input_boolean's contract requires a readable action_desc, and UI_add_verify_string's requires a readable test_buf, so fputs/strcmp never receive NULL.
A C caller passing a NULL action_desc or test_buf is outside the stated constructor contracts; the authority's fputs/strcmp would fault and this port does not extend validity to that input.

boundaries.mechanism: Console stream and terminal-state ownership: fopen(/dev/tty) with stdin/stderr fallback, TTY_IN/TTY_OUT/TTY_ORIG/TTY_NEW/IS_A_TTY, tcgetattr/tcsetattr, fclose identity guards, and the session lock.
boundaries.disposition: SAFETY_DISCHARGED (scope: one console session per process; src/ui/ui_openssl.rs:399-515)
boundaries.contract: open_console holds the UI's lock, sets both stream pointers unconditionally (fopen or the process stream), and installs TTY_ORIG only when tcgetattr succeeds. close_console is reached only after a successful open, and fcloses a stream only when it is not the process's stdin/stderr; both pointers are non-NULL on every successful path, so no NULL close and no double close of the process streams can occur. is_a_tty gates tcsetattr so a redirected stdin never receives it. Every remaining unsafe operation (static access, fopen/fclose/fileno/tcgetattr/tcsetattr/memcpy) has a stated validity contract at its site.

boundaries.mechanism: Signal-handler reentrancy edge: pushsig/popsig over 1..NX509_SIG-1, SAVSIG, PS, and recsig's storage of the signal number.
boundaries.contract: recsig runs at an arbitrary instruction on any thread and performs exactly one relaxed store into INTR_SIGNAL, an AtomicI32; it touches no allocation, lock, FILE, SAVSIG entry or other static. INTR_SIGNAL is no longer a `static mut`, so the handler cannot participate in a Rust data race. SAVSIG and PS are written only by the main thread inside one serialized session; the handler never reads them. The push/pop table is filled before PS=1 and read only when PS>=1, so a partially installed table is never restored.

boundaries.mechanism: Prompt/read/write callback buffer lifecycle: write_string, read_string, read_till_nl, read_string_inner, read_string_inner_error, UI_set_result, the 8192-byte result buffer and the over-long-line tail buffer.
boundaries.disposition: SAFETY_DISCHARGED (scope: the callback buffer extents and cleansing; src/ui/ui_openssl.rs:138-220, 238-255, 269-378)
boundaries.contract: fgets receives maxsize 8191 into an 8192-byte array, so it writes at most 8190 bytes plus NUL; the newline is replaced in place only when the pointer is inside that array; read_till_nl passes 4 into a 5-byte array (3 bytes plus NUL) and its chunk is now cleansed on both exits; the error label cleanses the full 8192 bytes on every success and failure path, and there is no return from read_string_inner that bypasses it. UI_set_result is called with a NUL-terminated result. The callback string preconditions are the constructors' (non-NULL prompt/action/test).

boundaries.mechanism: Process-global method registry: UI_OPENSSL, DEFAULT_UI_METH, UI_OpenSSL, UI_get_default_method, UI_set_default_method.
boundaries.disposition: CONTRACTED (scope: src/ui/ui_openssl.rs:583-651). The object has 'static lifetime and its name points at a 'static literal; the registry cell and the object's mutation ordering are protected only by stated caller obligations, not by a design mechanism and not by an independent dynamic check.
boundaries.contract: UI_OpenSSL answers a *mut to the one 'static method object; UI_get_default_method answers the current default and UI_set_default_method replaces it with a plain unsynchronised store. The authority's own manual binds this setter ('not thread-safe and should not be called at the same time as other OpenSSL functions'). Concurrent mutation of the shared object, or a read concurrent with the setter, is a data race and is excluded by the stated external contract. No safe-Rust interface returns or consumes these pointers.

caller_closure.disposition: SAFE (unchanged); its opener-failure early return is the precondition for B29-R1
caller_closure.evidence: UI_process calls open_session first and returns -1 without calling close_session when it refuses; on every other return it funnels through ui_process_err, which calls close_session. It passes a live ui and a live queue element to each callback. The console callbacks are never exported directly.

UI_set_result copies the NUL-terminated result into the caller's result buffer under the element's maxsize; the console method supplies result as an 8192-byte NUL-terminated array. The verify comparison then reads UI_get0_result_string and UI_get0_test_string, both of which the constructor contracts make non-NULL.

general_allocate_prompt rejects a NULL prompt and a NULL result_buf for prompt types, so out_string is non-NULL for every type; the verify and boolean constructors' own Safety contracts require a readable test_buf and action_desc. Those are exactly the callback preconditions named at B29-UI-3.

The console method uses the same sys declarations as the BIO methods; their FFI contracts are unchanged. The duplicate local `static mut stdin` declaration was removed so the file consumes the one sys declaration.

The lock is the per-UI CryptoRwlock created by UI_new_method; open_session acquires it and close_session releases it. No application callback is invoked between those calls, so the non-reentrant lock is not held across a callback edge.

The edited concurrency mechanism is the handler's single relaxed atomic store; there is no lock or shared-ownership transition to model. The full threaded suite (--test-threads=4) is the only dynamic concurrency evidence and does not itself drive a console session.

hidden_obligations_note: Zero for the audited file. The one hidden obligation found (B29-D1) was a Rust data race between recsig and the reader, and it is eliminated: the handler can reach only an AtomicI32. Every remaining precondition is stated at its point of use and in the module header: one console session per process, the documented non-thread-safety of UI_set_default_method, mutation ordering for the shared 'static method object, callback ordering by UI_process, and the constructors' non-NULL string contracts. B29-R1..R6 are explicitly recorded residuals, not hidden obligations.
new_unsafe_assumptions_note: None. The atomic conversion removes assumptions; the cleansing call adds no pointer, alignment or lifetime assumption (the buffer is a local array). The test-only sigaction/raise/tmpfile/rewind declarations are cfg(test) and never in a release build.
unsafe_operations_removed_detail: The write before pushsig (read_string_inner), the load in the error label, and the store in recsig were `unsafe { static mut INTR_SIGNAL ... }` operations. AtomicI32 store/load are safe Rust, and recsig's body now contains no unsafe operation at all. The duplicate extern `static mut stdin` declaration was also removed (a declaration, not an operation).
unsafe_operations_introduced_detail: OPENSSL_cleanse over the five-byte read_till_nl chunk, with a SAFETY comment naming the local array. Net production unsafe operations: -2.
test_only_unsafe_note: Two #[cfg(test)] tests add ten unsafe expressions: UI_OpenSSL/UI_new_method/UI_free, sigaction install and restore, raise, read_string_inner_error, tmpfile, fputs/rewind, read_till_nl and fclose. The raise/tmpfile/rewind externs are declared inside the test module.
boundary_size: 1 production file, src/ui/ui_openssl.rs (+174/-29), plus two test-only tests and the ledger/receipt updates. The production edits are: the module's concurrency and signal-edge contracts, INTR_SIGNAL→AtomicI32 at four sites, the read_till_nl restructure with cleansing, the callback preconditions, the open_console B29-R1 note, the registry mutation contract, removal of the duplicate stdin declaration, and the target_has_atomic gate.
safe_callers_can_cause_ub_note: No safe-Rust interface reaches this file: UI_OpenSSL, UI_get_default_method, UI_set_default_method, UI_new_method/UI_process and the constructors are unsafe extern "C" with stated contracts, and the callback functions are private. A C caller that violates the stated serialization or mutation preconditions is outside the ABI contract; a caller that honours them cannot reach UB through this file. B29-D1 was the only path by which a compliant caller could reach UB, and it is closed.

residuals.description: open_console:424-431 returns 0 on an errno outside the six admitted values with the per-UI lock still held and both /dev/tty streams open; UI_process then returns -1 without calling close_console. The authority does the same at ui_openssl.c:449-460. The path requires an exotic tcgetattr errno; no invalid release or dangling pointer results.

pushsig:540 ignores sigaction's answer. If an install fails, SAVSIG[i] stays zero and popsig:564 installs a zeroed SigAction (SIG_DFL, empty mask) for that signal instead of the previous disposition. The authority ignores the same return. No memory unsafety.

residuals.disposition: RETAINED authority-parity timing property; dudect/ctgrind NOT_RUN
residuals.description: read_string:212 compares the two entered strings with strcmp, which is data-dependent and early-exit. The authority does the same. This is a local verify prompt, not a cryptographic check, but no constant-time claim is made and no timing instrument was run.

pushsig installs recsig for synchronous fault signals (SIGSEGV, SIGBUS, SIGFPE, SIGILL) as well as asynchronous ones, exactly as the authority does. A synchronous fault returns to the faulting instruction; this is an authority-parity loop, not memory unsafety.

The streams, terminal states, SAVSIG and PS are process-global. Concurrent console sessions would race on them; the module header and open_console's contract require one session per process. This is the same serialisation the authority's unsynchronised globals require, and it is now an explicit precondition rather than a hidden assumption.

UI_OpenSSL:618 hands out a *mut to the same 'static object UI_get_default_method shares. Mutating it while any thread drives a UI over it is a data race; the export's contract requires mutation to be ordered before publication. No safe-Rust interface exposes the pointer.
